chunks: “Indeed, I dislike janabah (ritual impurity) when the sun turns yellow and when it rises while it is yellow.”

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike; indicates karahah or disapproved status
key_terms.إِنِّي: Indeed I; an emphatic first-person expression
key_terms.اَلْجَنَابَةَ: the state of janabah; ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.تَصْفَرُّ: turns yellow; describing the sun near sunset
key_terms.صَفْرَاءُ: yellow; describing the appearance of the sun

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to remain in a state of janabah at sunrise or sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys the dislike of remaining in a state of janabah at two specific times: when the sun yellows toward sunset and when it rises yellow at sunrise. It relates to ritual purity and indicates an emphasized etiquette connected to the timing of ghusl for janabah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: 'I dislike being in a state of janabah (ritual impurity) when the sun turns yellow (at sunset) and when it rises while it is yellow (sunrise)."
